With November elections quickly approaching, Mr Trump is also facing renewed domestic scrutiny over the war's costs on US consumers and toll on the military. stories.summary: Dublin and California-headquartered payments firm Stripe said it had agreed to buy OpenRouter, which helps businesses route and optimise token usage, its latest bet on the fast-growing AI industry. While the companies did not disclose the value of the deal, a source familiar with the matter, who requested anonymity to discuss confidential information, told Reuters it was worth slightly more than $8 billion. The deal comes as soaring bills drive companies toward cheaper models and routing tools like OpenRouter, and deepens a year-long push by the fintech into AI. The push has included launching products like token billing to track AI model consumption. AI marketplace platforms like OpenRouter allow developers to send queries to dozens of AI models through a single interface, making them a popular testing ground for new systems.

stories.title: Evacuation orders lifted in Belgian wildfire zone
stories.summary: Authorities in Belgium and Germany lifted the last remaining evacuation orders in the border region where firefighters appeared to be gaining the upper hand against the massive High Fens wildfire. After being grounded by bad weather, water-dropping aircraft were back out helping to quell Belgium's largest wildfire in a century, after fire crews hacked their way through boggy terrain overnight to fully "encircle" the blaze. Crisis cell spokesman Tony Hosmans said the fire burning since Friday "has been contained and should no longer be able to spread" - after threatening to spill over the German border to the east. New flare-ups were still emerging across the vast site - with the blaze smouldering underground in the peaty soil - but were being "brought under control" one by one, he said, with the next goal to finally tame the fire.

stories.summary: Ireland women's hockey captain Sarah Hawkshaw believes that all the pressure is on Belgium ahead of their crucial World Cup Pool C decider. A 3-2 victory over New Zealand on Tuesday keeps Ireland's qualification hopes alive. With the top two teams going through to the second round, Ireland must get a win against tournament hosts Belgium to avoid the 9th–16th classification games. Ireland will be the underdogs going into the game in front of a partisan Belgian crowd in Wavre, and they narrowly lost two Pro League games 2-1 to them in Dublin last December.

stories.summary: The AFL's Irish experiment nearly failed before even it really even began - and it all came down to a split-second decision in the 1987 Victorian Football League preliminary final between Melbourne and Hawthorn. The VFL was three years from morphing into the AFL and a huge crowd had gathered to watch what turned into a manic final quarter with tennis legend Pat Cash even interrupting a family holiday to attend. Melbourne missed chance after chance to kill off the Hawks’ challenge in the final minutes of the match, Simon Eishold’s incredible mis-hit hook behind long remembered by Demons fans, but it was the final play that saw it go down in infamy and left recently-recruited Dubliner Jim Stynes labelled as a laughing stock. Kept alive by Melbourne’s inefficiency, Gary Buckenara was given one last chance to win it from Hawthorn but from way out, it was a low percentage chance.

stories.title: FIFA sacking Lamour sends 'troubling message' - UEFA VP
stories.summary: FIFA's decision to dismiss senior executive Kevin Lamour sends a "deeply troubling message to all of us seeking change", UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister has said. FIFA confirmed Lamour’s departure as chief operating officer on Monday evening, just over two weeks after he released a statement to the Associated Press saying the FIFA administration had been "deceived" by president Gianni Infantino over a plan to sell stakes in a World Cup company to private investors. Lamour’s statement on 31 July, along with the resignation of senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro earlier the same day, heaped further pressure on Infantino, with Lamour describing the private investor plan as "the project of one person". Now UEFA executive committee member McAllister, a former Wales captain who worked with Lamour at European football’s governing body when he was its deputy general secretary, has spoken out to criticise his sacking.

stories.title: Something for the Weekend: The Jimmy Cake's cultural picks
stories.summary: To celebrate the 25th anniversary of their seminal debut album, Brains, The Jimmy Cake will play the album in full - in their first concert in just under a decade at the National Concert Hall this November. The band formed in Dublin in the late 1990s and Brains announced their arrival proper. As a nine-piece blending accordion, clarinet, saxophone, glockenspiel, trumpet and DIY percussion around the core of guitars, bass and drums they went on to release lauded efforts such as 2002’s Dublin Gone. Everybody Dead and 2008’s Spectre and Crown before later albums Master (2015) and Tough Love (2017). Parallel to his involvement with The Jimmy Cake, pianist, synthesist, graphic designer and label manager Paul G Smyth has also set himself apart as a singular voice in Europe’s vigorous improvised music scene, working with luminaries such as Derek Bailey, Evan Parker, Peter Brötzmann and Keiji Haino. I’m being quietly haunted by a film from 2019 called I’m No Longer Here. Written and directed by Fernando Frías de la Parra, it follows an exiled Mexican teenager obsessed with slowed-down cumbia music struggling to adapt in New York after fleeing cartel violence. There’s something unspoken in it that has held me since and I don’t know what it is. "I think I know what it is," my wife said recently as she left the room. That’s helpful, isn’t it?

With a focus on health, natural beauty and minimalism (albeit through the skewed lens of Western beauty standards...), the 'clean girl aesthetic' appeared in 2020, becoming a lifestyle trend enthusiastically endorsed and proliferated on social media, particularly TikTok. You'll no doubt have seen versions of it: the dewy skin, the glossy blush, the barely there mascara and impeccably groomed brows, all topped off with a shiny slicked-back bun.

The inspection, which occurred in April, followed a cautionary meeting with the provider the previous month due to medicine management practices and other issues.

stories.summary: More than 500 people have applied for the Stardust payment scheme set up for survivors of the fire, according to the latest figures from the Department of Justice. The scheme was established last February and will see successful applicants receive a €20,000 payment for "delays in providing truth and justice". The department said 540 people have so far applied, with 169 of them validated and authorised for payment. It said further applications are proceeding towards final validation and this number is expected to increase in the coming weeks.

stories.title: China Evergrande founder sentenced to life in prison
stories.summary: The founder of China Evergrande Group, the world's most-indebted property developer, was sentenced to life in prison by a Chinese court today, five years after the firm's collapse shook the nation's economy and financial markets. Hui Ka Yan, once Asia's richest man, pleaded guilty in April to eight charges, including misuse of funds, fundraising fraud, illegally taking public deposits, illegally extending loans, fraudulently issuing securities and bribery. Evergrande, once China's premier developer, has defaulted on most of its $300 billion in liabilities, its troubles symbolising a crisis in the property sector that has long dragged on the world's second-biggest economy. The sentence in the southern city of Shenzhen, which included confiscating all of Hui's personal property, ends his rags-to-riches story but is unlikely to bring much solace to Evergrande's domestic and foreign creditors.

The only previous times soccer had been played at the venue were between 2007 and 2009 when it served as the temporary home of the Republic of Ireland during the redevelopment of Lansdowne Road. But Peter McKenna, Croke Park’s stadium and commercial director, is keen to change that to find new revenue streams to put into the GAA.

stories.title: Mean Girls: How Tina Fey's teen classic became a cultural icon
stories.summary: Teenagers of the 80s had the oeuvre of filmmaker John Hughes to school them through the most painful moments of their adolescence. Teens in the 90s had pop adaptations of classics like Clueless (based on Jane Austen's Emma) or Ten Things I Hate About You (a sexy version of Shakespeare’s The Taming of the Shrew). For those coming of age in the early naughties, however, there was only one film in town: Mean Girls, the movie that launched the career of its stars Lindsay Lohan and Rachel McAdams, as well as its writer and co-star Tina Fey. I had already finished college when Mean Girls was released, but its anatomisation of the rigid social hierarchies were recognisable - and cathartically appealing - to anyone who had survived the brutal years of adolescence since teenagehood was first recognised in popular culture, in the post-World War Two period. Tina Fey herself was in her 30s when she wrote Mean Girls, catapulting her from small-screen supporting roles on and off the Saturday Night Live circuit into the glaring limelight of Hollywood. Formally, the film was an adaptation of a popular self-help title, Queen Bees and Wannabes by Rosalind Wiseman, which was written as a supportive guide for parents navigating the dangerous playground of the middle years with their teenagers, but Fey also drew heavily on her own experience of high school in Pennsylvania in the 1980s. The intermittent voiceover, narrated by Lohan, who plays Cady - a homeschooled maths-whizz who finds herself thrown headfirst into the savage ecosystem of her peers when she enrols in her local high school - might well be the voice of Fey herself.

stories.title: Dublin's newest street mural honours the women of the Monto
stories.summary:
In a side street off Talbot St, a vibrant new mural is shedding light on the women of Monto, once one of Europe's largest red-light districts during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, bringing to life a rich but often forgotten part of Dublin's history. Muralist Holly Pereira has painted the striking artwork on Mabbot Lane, a small section of street that features in James Joyce's Ulysses, described as "the entrance to Nighttown". I have been practising as a muralist for 11 years, having worked as an illustrator before that. The first big mural I painted was coming up to Repeal the 8th referendum in 2016. From that moment, I was hooked on the scale, vibrancy and potential for communication within murals.

What drew you to the history of the Monto and the women who worked there? I have always been interested in feminism, women's history and the histories of marginalised communities. Having lived in Dublin for many years, I was surprised to learn about Monto only five years ago. It baffled me that such a significant part of Dublin’s history could be so little known.

stories.title: 79% of adults interested in new savings scheme - research
stories.summary: The vast majority of adults in Ireland (79%) are interested in investing in the Government's new planned Savings and Investment Account, research from the Banking & Payments Federation Ireland (BPFI) suggests. According to the BPFI survey, almost half of adults (48%) are aware of the scheme, although this drops to 25% of younger adults aged 18-34.

stories.title: Why bad workplace meetings can harm your wellbeing
stories.summary: Analysis: Some of us can spend up to 23 hours a week in pointless meetings, all of which reflect an organisation's culture, dynamics and priorities Anyone working in an organisation knows it: meetings follow one after another at a frantic pace. On average, managers spend 23 hours a week in meetings. Much of what happens in them is considered to be of low value, or even entirely counterproductive. The paradox is that bad meetings generate even more meetings in an attempt to repair the damage caused by previous ones. For a long time, meetings were not subject of management research. A 2015 handbook laid the groundwork for the nascent field of meeting science. Among other things, the research showed that the real issue may not be the number of meetings, but rather how they are designed, the lack of clarity about their purpose, and the inequalities they (often unconsciously) reinforce. In our series of studies conducted during and after the Covid-19 pandemic, researchers found that meetings can both foster and harm participants' wellbeing. Indeed, participating in too many meetings can lead to burn-out and an intention to quit the organisation; however, meetings can also increase employee engagement.

stories.summary: When Mikel Arteta leads Arsenal out at home to Coventry on Friday evening, he will do so as the longest serving manager in the Premier League. Fresh from getting Arsenal over the line to their first league title in more than two decades, Arteta is now the elder statesman of the league after Pep Guardiola decided to call time on his 10 years with Manchester City. The next trick for Arteta is to defend the title and win back-to-back Premier Leagues for the first time in the club's history, surpassing even the achievements of Arsene Wenger. Arsenal go into the season as the heavy favourites. A sense of uncertainty and flux settles in over their rivals, while Arteta’s steady hand, long-term squad building and continued improvement means they’re the team to beat.

stories.title: Offaly's All-Ireland winning captain Pádraig Horan dies
stories.summary: Pádraig Horan, who captained Offaly to their first All-Ireland hurling success in 1981, has died at the age of 76 after a long battle with illness. In a lengthy inter-county career which began at the end of the 1960s, Horan was to the fore as the Faithful famously shocked Kilkenny to win a maiden Leinster title in 1980s. Offaly had arrived, with the St Ryangh's clubman adding three more provincial crowns and another Liam MacCarthy success, in 1985, to his collection. His exploits on the field, first as a defender before moving to the full-forward berth, were also recognised when he was named on the All-Star team for '85. As a coach, he managed Offaly to win a National League title in 1991, while four years later he was at the helm when Birr landed All-Ireland senior club honours.
